h1: UK amusement arcades and places to play
intro: Lights, games and somebody who is certain they can win that cuddly toy. Find seaside amusements, family arcades and other gaming venues around the UK. Open a venue card for its own guide, and check the venue type before taking children. There is always room for a little play time.

featured.title: Silcocks Family Arcade and Late Lounge
featured.text: We visited Silcock’s Late Lounge on Nevill Street and found older fruit machines, newer cabinets and a lovely welcome from the staff — drinks, biscuits and plenty to look round. My Raider Score is 4.7/5 for the September 2026 lounge visit. The wider premises have family amusements; the Late Lounge is strictly 18+.

editorial_html:
Lights, laughs and a little time to play

You hear it before you see it: the games, the coins and somebody having a very good go at something. UK amusement arcades make a fun stop on a seaside day or a trip into town. Browse the venue guides and see where you fancy a look round. Family amusements and adult-only venues are different places, so choose the one that suits your group. Add the beach, a food stop or another attraction and make a day of it.

What you'll find inside

  • Coin pushers – the classic 2p and 10p falls, often stacked with novelty prizes, keyrings and tokens.

  • Cranes and prize machines – grabbers, stackers and "win every time" machines with plush toys and gadgets.

  • Ticket games – skee-ball, wheel spinners and video redemption games that spit out tickets you swap at the prize counter.

  • Video games and simulators – racing cabinets, shooting games, air hockey and basketball hoops.

  • Retro corners – plenty of seaside arcades keep a few vintage cabinets or old-school pushers for the nostalgia crowd.

Picking the right arcade for your crowd

Got little ones? Look for a family arcade with a clear prize counter and plenty of low-stake pushers. Teenagers usually head straight for the driving games and dance machines. Big kids who grew up in the eighties might fancy a town with a dedicated retro room. Most arcades are indoors, which makes them a lifesaver when the British weather turns, and the bigger seaside halls are usually step-free with wide aisles, though older buildings can be a squeeze.

Famous arcade towns include Blackpool, Great Yarmouth, Skegness, Cleethorpes, Scarborough, Southend, Margate and Weston-super-Mare, where the seafront is practically one long run of flashing lights.

Tips for getting the most from your coppers

  • Set a spending pot before you go in and split it into bags for the kids – it stops the "just one more go" spiral.

  • Bring a pouch of 2p coins, although most places have change machines and many now take cards on token systems.

  • Save tickets across visits: plenty of arcades let you keep a ticket card, so you can build up to the big prize.

  • Go early on a sunny day or late afternoon on a rainy one – that's when everyone else piles in.

  • Under-18s should stick to the family side; anything marked as an adult area is off limits.

Ready to hit the seafront? Scroll back up to the cards above for arcades worth a visit, then hop over to the town pages to see what else is around once your coppers run out.
